Messages.Author: Walter Denny
Messages.Body:
I have not played in a while. Where I played the table rules were when a
person left play he took his cards. As you relalize this could really hurt
a corruption deck. If I spend all my time taking his vampires just to have
him take them back when I oust him. Is this standard play in most games?
What are the official rules?

Messages.Author: pie...@my-deja.com
Messages.Body:
"Walter Denny" <rd...@email.msn.com> wrote:
> I have not played in a while. Where I played the table
> rules were when a person left play he took his cards.

From the Revised Rulebook:
|1.3. The Golden Rule of Card Ownership
|Your cards are never transferred to another player permanently
|as a result of card play. At the end of the game, the cards you
|began the game with are returned to you. If you are ousted, all
|the cards you control are burned. Any of your opponents' cards
|you may control are placed in their respective owners' ash
|heaps (see Important Terms, sec. 1.1). Any of your cards that
|other players control remain until the controlling players are
|ousted. The only exception to this rule is the optional ante
|(see Playing for Ante, sec. 2.4): ante cards may change
|hands permanently.

So after you oust your prey, you keep his vamps in your controlled
region. Otherwise Followers of Set are pretty well useless.

Having played a corruption deck at a tournament, I can say that they
can be extremely effective. BTW - I made it to the finals and was
summarily removed from play by the other four players (Bleed, Cross
table bleed, vote and rush) since they knew that once I reached
critical mass there was no stopping the onrushing hordes.

Stu
-Your Friendly Neighborhood Camarilla Scholar

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Walter Denny wrote:
>
> I have not played in a while. Where I played the table rules were when a

> person left play he took his cards. As you relalize this could really hurt
> a corruption deck. If I spend all my time taking his vampires just to have
> him take them back when I oust him. Is this standard play in most games?
> What are the official rules?

1.3. The Golden Rule of Card Ownership

Your cards are never transferred to another player permanently as a result
of card play. At the end of the game, the cards you began the game with are
returned to you. If you are ousted, all the cards you control are burned.
Any of your opponents' cards you may control are placed in their respective
owners' ash heaps (see Important Terms, sec. 1.1). Any of your cards that
other players control remain until the controlling players are ousted.
